transcript: The other night, Paul and I saw The Wiz on Broadway. This revival is a wonderful vocal showcase but I thought it could have used a bit more oomph from the production standpoint. We saw Mariah Lyttle go on as Dorothy and she was fantastic as was the rest of the cast. Avery Wilson as the scarecrow was the showstopping highlight for me. His performance was so much fun and remarkably impressive from a vocal standpoint. This musical is beloved for good reason — the story, although familiar, is quite charming and the music is wonderful. In this production, I really loved the characterization of Dorothy's three companions, but the direction otherwise felt a little scattered at times. I think that the relatively barebones set featuring a big screen of animated projections did not help this. To me, the shortages in the production value is precisely what held the show back from being this big and glorious Wiz revival that I was hoping for but I still found it quite enjoyable and the performances certainly carried. With that, another playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer enjoyed the show and found it 'quite enjoyable' with standout performances, but had notable reservations about production value and direction that prevented it from meeting expectations.
